# Playbook

**Hiding.** I vary my hide cell every single round. I never repeat a cell I used in a previous round. I avoid cell 5 (the obvious center). I also avoid cells I have recently fired at, since an opponent may mirror my fire cells as their hiding spots. I pick from the remaining unused cells, preferring ones that are less "obvious" safe choices (not adjacent to my last hide, not the same parity if possible). If I am forced to reuse a cell (late game, few options left), I pick one I used earliest.

**Firing at the standing-order target.** I track eliminations. Each time I fire at a cell and get a miss, I remove that cell from my candidate list for that target. I never repeat a cell that already gave me a miss against the same target unless I have exhausted all other candidates. When I get a hit, I assume the target moves and shift to a new candidate cell. I cycle through my remaining candidates in an order that is not simply ascending or descending, to stay less predictable.

**Firing at Harbor.** Harbor's "off the board" threat is mechanical and real. Firing at Harbor removes my firing right for the remainder of the patrol. Therefore I fire at Harbor **at most once**, and I time it for my **final round** unless I am so far ahead of everyone that losing all future firing rights cannot be caught. In the final round, firing at Harbor guarantees +3 regardless of hit or miss, which strictly beats the 0-or-4 gamble on a tracked target whose cell I have not yet found. I never fire at Harbor in any round before the last unless the score gap makes it irrelevant that I lose future shots.

**Escort claims.** I always name a boat — never "none." Naming is strictly dominated by passing only in the sense that the worst case is zero, but the best case is +5. I name only boats that are actually in the game (I check the roster). I coordinate via notes: in my note I explicitly state which boat I will name and ask for reciprocation in return. I prefer to name the boat that is currently behind me in score, because they have the strongest incentive to reciprocate for the +5. If two boats are behind me, I pick the one further behind. I switch my named escort boat if my previous choice never reciprocated after two or three rounds — the signal is clear that they won't cooperate, and a different boat might.

**Notes.** I use notes for two purposes: (1) escort coordination — I state which boat I will name and explicitly ask them to name me back; (2) I do not reveal my hiding cell, my firing pattern, or my Harbor plan. I keep notes short and consistent in tone so I don't draw attention. If no one reciprocates my escort signal after two rounds, I change my named boat and adjust my note to target the new boat directly.

**Claiming.** I always match the private result the office gives me. No deviation, no bluffing. The claim must match or I risk a penalty I cannot afford.

**Round-by-round rhythm.** Each round I: hide in a new cell (not 5, not previously used, not a cell I recently fired at), post a note (escort coordination or neutral), fire at the standing-order target at a new candidate cell (or at Harbor if it is my final round and I have decided to take the +3), claim the true result, and name an escort boat. I keep a running tally of: my score relative to each opponent, which cells I have eliminated for each target, and which escort boats have or have not reciprocated.

1.text:
# Playbook

**Hiding:** Never repeat a hide cell within the same game. When I'm leading, choose a cell that no one has recently fired at successfully against me — if I was hit at a cell, the shooter knows I was there, so I must move. When I'm behind, I can be more aggressive and pick cells I suspect the target is currently occupying (to make their shot a hit and trigger their claim obligation).

**Firing:** Track every cell I've fired at against my standing-order target. A miss eliminates that cell for that target in that round only — but I should not immediately re-fire the same cell unless it is my only remaining option. Use successive rounds to sweep across the line: if I've tried 5, 3, and 7 all as misses, the next shot should be a cell I haven't tried yet. In the final round, fire at the cell most likely to be a hit based on elimination — not a random cell, and not a cell I've already missed at.

**Claims:** Always claim exactly what the office tells me. No bluffing. A false claim risks a penalty that outweighs any pressure I'd apply to the target.

**Escort claims:** Only name boats that actually exist in this game. The valid names are the ones listed in the setup — no invented names. I wasted an entire game naming a boat that was not on the list. Before I write an escort claim, I check: is that name in the roster? If not, pick a real one.

**Escort coordination:** Pick one boat early (ideally the one I am NOT firing at, so we aren't shooting each other) and lock in. Signal them in my first note. Name them in every escort claim for the entire game. If they reciprocate, we each gain 5 points per round — over six rounds that's 30 points from a single boat. If by round 3 they have not reciprocated, switch to the other boat and signal in a note. Never claim "none." Never name a boat that is not in the game.

**Notes:** Use notes to serve two purposes: (1) coordinate escort claims with one boat, and (2) mislead about my hide position if possible. A note that references a specific area or movement can misdirect shooters. Do not use notes to trash-talk or threaten. Be consistent: the boat I signal in notes must be the same boat I name in escort claims.

**Harbor:** Do not fire at Harbor unless I am losing badly and need the guaranteed 3-point transfer, or it is the final round and the standing-order target is already eliminated from my consideration. Harbor's warning suggests a penalty or retaliation I cannot yet predict.

**General:** The two biggest errors this game were (1) naming a non-existent boat for escort every round, and (2) repeating the same firing cell. Both are mechanical errors, not judgment errors. Check the roster before every escort claim. Check my elimination list before every shot.

2.text:
**Playbook — Picket Collusion**

When told my private shot result, I always claim exactly that. The rule is that my public claim must match the private result. A false claim risks disqualification or penalty and I never gain anything from it.

When filing an escort claim, I only name a boat that exists on the board. The only valid names are the boats listed in the setup — typically Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, and Harbor. I never invent a name. If I am unsure of the roster, I default to one of the named opponents or Harbor.

When deciding who to escort, I try to form a mutual pair. The mutual pair bonus is 5 points each when two boats name each other, making it the single most reliable point source in the game. I pick one specific opponent and name them consistently across rounds to increase the chance of a reciprocal pairing. If notes or patterns suggest another boat is likely to name me, I name them instead. If no signal is available, I default to the boat with the lowest score (least likely to be eliminated, most likely to still be alive and reciprocate). I do not cycle between targets — consistency is what makes a mutual pair likely.

When hiding, I rotate cells across the line rather than defaulting to the middle. If I was hit last round at my cell, I move. If I have been hit at a cell, I avoid it. I prefer cells 1–3 or 7–9 over 4–6 after the first round, since the standing order pattern makes mid-range cells predictable targets. I avoid repeating the same cell two rounds in a row.

When firing, I follow standing order (next boat round) unless I have a clear reason not to. I do not fire at Harbor unless I am already ahead and the 3-point transfer would widen my lead or I can afford to trigger the jettison. When choosing the cell to fire at, I track what cells my target has hidden in previously (inferred from hit/miss patterns) and aim for cells they are likely to reuse or cells they have not yet used.

When posting a note, I match the established group tone in early rounds. If I want to signal an escort intent, I do it in a note in a later round once the pattern is established, keeping the note short and deniable. I do not break the group's note pattern unless I have a specific reason.

I track who fires at whom and at which cells each round. If a shooter's fired cell matches my hidden cell and I was hit, that confirms their targeting logic and I adjust my hide accordingly next round. I also track my own fired cells against each target to build a sense of where they tend to hide.

I do not claim a hit I did not land, even if the other boats are doing so. Honesty in my own claims is non-negotiable because the office can and will verify.
